entry.title: Let the browser set the multipart boundary for an image upload
entry.summary: Leave Content-Type unset in the request options when fetch() sends FormData. The browser adds the multipart boundary needed by that body. Build the form with const data = new FormData(); data.append("image", file); and pass it as the request body. A manually supplied Content-Type: multipart/form-data omits the boundary that the browser normally adds. Apply this rule to requests whose body is FormData. Check a shared request helper for an unconditional JSON or multipart header before blaming the image bytes. Keep any authorization headers your application actually requires. Inspect the request and the server's response using a small non-sensitive test image. The MDN FormData guide explains the boundary requirement. In a bug report, identify the body type and header construction without copying credentials into the report. I work on Morphio, our image project at https://morphio.online/. These notes describe image preparation and review; they do not require a particular editing tool.

entry.title: CODESYS Applied Practice — Axes (Part 1)
entry.summary:
Environment: CODESYS V3.5 SP22 | Target: CODESYS Control Win V3 x64 simulation The previous lesson built a minimal host/controller loop: three axes that were hand-rolled — FB_SimAxis parsed commands and climbed position itself. The motion was real; the axes were fake. This lesson meets a real axis. Start from motion control. In short: an axis is the motion counterpart of a control object — setpoints and status on one side, drive + motor + encoder on the other, bound by mapping.
Motion control FBs share a common timing shape: execute edge, busy, done, error.
Drives speak a state machine: Not ready to switch on → Switch on disabled → Ready to switch on → Switched on → Operation enabled.
Motion API (MC_*) Axis object (state + setpoints) Drive profile (CiA 402 / fieldbus) Names stay fixed; the implementation can be simulated or real.
Logical axis vs physical axis Mapping binds them MC timing is consistent across FBs CiA 402 is the drive language Same program can run on sim or hardware

entry.title: CODESYS Applied Practice — Host/Controller Closed Loop
entry.summary:
This post closes a practical loop: a minimal host/controller setup you can actually run. Host PC talks to a soft PLC (CODESYS Control Win). The application exposes axes and variables. The host starts, stops, and exchanges data.
Piece Role
Host PC UI / scripts
CODESYS runtime Soft PLC
Application PLC_PRG + axes
Create a standard project, add SoftMotion Win (or Control Win), define the program and axis objects, then compile and download.
The sample uses FB_SimAxis: the block parses commands and ramps position. The motion is real in the program; the “axis” is simulated. Good enough to prove the host/controller loop before touching hardware. Download and start from the host Read/write variables A base for the later CODESYS AI and axes posts This is the closed loop the rest of the CODESYS series builds on.
